content: Acacia senegal, commonly referred to as Rudraksha, Gum Acacia, Gum Arabic Tree, or Gum Senegal Tree, is a small deciduous tree. It is native to semi-desert regions of Sub-Saharan Africa, as well as Oman, Pakistan, and northwestern India. The tree typically grows to a height of 5 to 12 meters, with a trunk diameter of up to 30 centimeters. Uses Forage The fresh foliage of Acacia senegal is highly valuable as forage for livestock. Food The dried seeds of the tree are consumed as food by humans. Gum Arabic Acacia senegal produces gum arabic, a natural product widely used as a food additive, in various crafts, and in cosmetics. The gum is harvested by making incisions in the tree's bark, with each tree yielding approximately 200 to 300 grams of gum. Notably, Sudan is responsible for producing 70% of the world's supply of gum arabic. Medicinal Uses The gum from Acacia senegal is utilized for its soothing effects on the mucous membranes of the intestines and for treating inflamed skin. Additionally, it is reported to have astringent properties and is used in the treatment of bleeding, bronchitis, diarrhea, gonorrhea, leprosy, typhoid fever, and upper respiratory tract infections. Rope The roots of the tree, which are located near the surface of the ground, are highly effective for crafting strong ropes and cords. The bark of the tree is also used in rope-making. Wood The wood of Acacia senegal is employed in the production of tool handles and components for weaving looms. Botanical Variations There are several botanical varieties of Acacia senegal, including: Acacia senegal var. leiocarpa Brenan Acacia senegal var. rostrata Brenan
